descriptor.scene: There is no human being in this frame and no second capped mascot figure. The camera is well back and THE MACHINERY IS THE SUBJECT: a wide interior of the glowing machine at full working hum. Three things read clearly. RAILS: polished brass-and-wood rails run in long parallel curves across the floor and away to the right, small cream carriages sitting on them. A GATE: a low honey-wood gate stands across one rail in the middle distance, its simple bar down, one warm amber lamp lit above it. A CANON: along the left wall, a tall built-in shelf of pale wood, many shelves deep, filled with small neat cream boxes and slim bound books, orderly and plainly well used. Between them half a dozen small rounded cream machines run quietly, each with one simple dial, soft hum lines rising. The manager is small at his post on a low wooden platform in the middle distance, at full length and no taller than a third of the frame height, turned three-quarter with one mitten arm raised and extended toward the running machines, head up, weight forward. Warm honeyed light throughout, plum light pooling around him. Composition: shelf left, gate and rails centre, machines receding right; the top right stays calm warm wall.
descriptor._caption: His factory hums around him. Rails for the routine moves. Gates that refuse a bad step before it costs anything. A canon that remembers every taste June ever showed him. None of it was here on the first day. Every run that ever happened built some of it.
negatives: a human being of any kind
readable text or lettering on the books and boxes
